text:
tomas: FYI we're starting bring-up for pelican-6b (pulled from openrepo) and legal flagged the redistribution clause. wondering if we can ship a quantized serving-only variant (4-bit) behind Dedicated with strict no-download controls. :wave:

anya: Can you paste the exact license snippet? wording matters a lot here. :mag:

meera: Also have initial quant runs: 4-bit GPTQ on p4-dev — latency ~2.1x faster, top-1 accuracy on our intent test down ~1.2 pts, rouge-L -1.1 on summarization. Nothing catastrophic but need to check safety regression suite.

tomas: Snippet copied: ```
Redistribution: Model weights may not be redistributed for commercial purposes. Hosting the model to provide API-based inference is permitted provided the model binaries are not publicly distributed. Attribution: Any public product using the model must credit the Original Authors and link to the LICENSE.```

ben: That looks like "serve-only" friendly language (hosting allowed) but the "may not be redistributed" line still ambiguous for customer-hosted cases. If a customer chooses Dedicated with full disk access, that could be construed as redistribution. We should block giving customers direct access to files.

meera: Agreed. Our canary plan could be: internal canary -> Dedicated internal customers (with contractual restriction that they cannot export weights) -> if legal OK, broader. From perf-quality POV we should also produce a fall-back (fp16 unimpaired) route for cases with stricter quality.

anya: Ops note: pipeline currently retains a build artifact tarball for 30 days. Need a policy change to encrypt-and-hide downloads for license=restricted models, and to scrub any public buckets.

artifact-bot: Scan result for pelican-6b: discovered upload manifest tag "license: PRL-1" and artifact "pelican-6b-fp16.tar.gz" stored in s3://redwood-models/dev/pelican-6b/2026-03-21. Public ACL: false. Access logs available.

ben: Good catch. We should add an automatic post-ingest job to remove any secondary artifacts (quant files) from public buckets if license.restriction=true. I'll open a PR.

meera: Quick eval details uploaded: https://artifacts.internal/pelican-6b/quant-eval-2026-03-21.tsv — includes safety/regression diffs. Notable: safety classifier false positive rate +0.5, hallucination rate (precision) down 0.9%.

anya: Legal asked for a short memo of how we'll satisfy attribution. Proposed wording for product docs: "This product uses Pelican-6B (Pelican Research Team). Licensed under PRL-1. See LICENSE." We'll also add machine provenance header in responses and a required model-credit in Dedicated onboarding checklist. Is that sufficient?

legal-bot: Legal note (from counsel): "API serving is permitted under PRL-1 so long as the weight binaries are not redistributed. For Dedicated where the customer receives direct binary access, a commercial redistribution restriction may apply; require an exception or a different licensing agreement. Attribution as described is acceptable. Please record decision in Compliance tracker."

tomas: Thanks legal-bot. Action items: 1) Ben — PR to block artifact download/export for license=PRL-1 (and scrub public copies). 2) Meera — run full eval runbook and add prompt-level diff. 3) Anya — add attribution copy + provenance header spec to docs. 4) Legal team: brief memo and exception path for Dedicated customer-hosted requests.

ben: Opening PR now: https://git.internal/p/infra/artifacts/+/412 — adds metadata flagging and removes download links unless role in [security, compliance]. Also adds audit log entry for any access.

meera: Uploaded expanded evals and prompt diffs: https://artifacts.internal/pelican-6b/quant-eval-2026-03-21-full.csv — looking at where hallucination increase concentrates, will post a short write-up.

anya: Drafted provenance header: `X-Model-Provenance: pelican-6b;license=PRL-1;quantized=4bit;artifact_id=2026-03-21`. Also added attribution line for UI.

artifact-bot: Removal job scheduled for s3://redwood-models/dev/pelican-6b/2026-03-21/quant/*.tar.gz — job id 9981.

meera: One more note: QA suggests enabling fp16 fallback route for conversation workloads where safety regressions are sensitive. We'll include that in canary RFC.

legal-bot: Counsel update: "We can allow serve-only deployment for pelican-6b. For Dedicated customer-hosted scenarios, require a signed agreement that prohibits downstream redistribution; otherwise deny binary access."

tomas: Excellent. Closing loop: we'll proceed with internal canary and strict export controls + attribution. Keeping thread open until canary RFC merged. Thanks! :tada:
